topic: Swarm: Local-First Control Plane Watching Every Claude Code Session Live

key_points: Primary subject under review; 'See every agent. Stop the collisions.' Local-first control plane for AI-agent development on any repo.
One daemon watches every Claude Code (and Codex CLI, Gemini, Grok, Aider, opencode) session live: tool calls, reasoning, token spend, cost.
Keeps a ledger of who holds which task, worktree and runtime resource; turns CLAUDE.md 'never do X' prose into real permission decisions; streams all to one dashboard.
Runs entirely on your machine — no account, no telemetry, works offline, nothing added to repositories. Install: bunx @ra3orblade/swarm setup.

Early but real and shipping fast: eleven releases; observability across six agent CLIs, task claims in isolated worktrees, runtime resources, rules and incidents, cross-forge merge queue, spawned agents (swarm run / swarm dispatch), declarative workflows, verification gates w/ built-in reviewer, handoffs, agent-to-agent messaging, session replay, budgets, signed org policy, self-hosted team daemon.

Core screens: Fleet, Session (live reasoning stream + replay + resume-where-it-died), Board (tasks/worktrees/runtime resources/incidents), Rules (shared_tree, destructive_git, pattern_kill, protected_ports, no_foreign_worktree, claim_required_to_write, each ask|deny|off per repo in .swarm.toml), Run & Dispatch.
TypeScript/Bun, Apache-2.0, 6 stars, 1 fork, created 2026-08-20, topics incl. local-first, observability, orchestration, worktrees, claude-code.
SWAMERY — 'Run your Claude Code agents like a fleet, not like a pile of terminal tabs.' A local-first control plane for Claude Code sessions.
One Go binary, no cloud, no account; listens on :7777; data 100% local. Ships a versioned plugin marketplace so agents live in one place and every project pulls them with /plugin update.

See everything — every session live (tool calls, diffs, cost, sub-agents, errors); approve/deny permission prompts from one queue; auto-approve rule for recurring prompts; delegate headless agents in git worktrees run a card from Inbox through Working to Review with a verifier grading results; per-agent scorecards and rule-based advisor.
Quickstart: curl install; backfills from ~/.claude/projects JSONL transcripts — nothing to instrument; fail-open hooks shim; launchd service on macOS.
Go 1.25 binary + React 19 UI; control plane under PolyForm NC 1.0.0, framework Apache-2.0; 4 stars, 4 forks, created 2026-07-09.
Published 2026-07-20. Compared old vs new agent swarms building SQLite from scratch; found better coordination delivers similar quality at a fraction of the cost.
Browser swarm from earlier 2026 peaked at roughly 1,000 commits per hour on Git; the new system peaks at around 1,000 commits per second.
Stacked/layered review is high-return because review is much cheaper than the work it audits — compute spent on review is worthwhile, a major contributor to sustained quality.
Version-control system for agents; letting agents shape the environment; results vary across model mixes.
Addy Osmani, Feb 2026. Claude Code now supports first-class agent teams (swarms): a lead agent delegates to multiple parallel teammates that research, debug, and build while coordinating.
Community had been calling these patterns swarms — coordinated teams of specialist agents; what started as feature-flagged capabilities and bash-subagent workarounds is now a native feature.
TeammateTool, inbox-based communication, tmux split panes. Enable agent teams in settings.json.
Framing: fundamentally different architecture from the single-agent model; the shift from conductor to orchestrator is where parallel agent workflows become concrete.
'Claude Code's new hidden feature: Swarms' (521 pts, 335 comments, Jan 2026). Feature shipped in latest claude code builds but gated behind a feature flag that phones home to the backend.
Key theme: a team lead agent plans/delegates/synthesizes rather than writing code — context stays clean, subagents get fresh context leading to less token usage and better reasoning.

Debate: built-in Swarms vs third-party wrappers (Conductor, Gas Town, claude-flow, GSD/get-shit-done, mcp_agent_mail, Claude Code orchestrators). Difference cited = tightly integrated into the harness + delegation mode that clears lead-aggent context + mailbox system for subagent-to-subagent communication.
Privacy alarm: telemetry captures 'Claude session JSONL files (when accessible)' — complete conversation histories.
'Agent swarms and the new model economics' (278 pts, Jul 2026) — community discussion of Cursor's harness economics: delegation patterns cut token usage via fresh focused contexts.

Skepticism: only models trusted to work autonomously still cost more than a human employee; concern about reviewing copious generated code, maintaining conviction in large changesets (mitigated by automated reviewer agents).
View of the shift: human becomes reviewer/manager reviewing final changelist rather than every intermediate step; works in practice, not by hand-holding single agents.

stats.fact: ra3orblade/swarm — local-first control plane, TypeScript/Bun, Apache-2.0, 6 stars / 1 fork as of launch window, created 2026-08-20, eleven releases, observability across six agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini, Grok, Aider, opencode).
Swarm runs fully on-machine: no account, no telemetry, works offline, adds nothing to your repositories. Install via `bunx @ra3orblade/swarm setup`.

Swarm rules guardrails target Bash commands a Claude Code session runs: shared_tree, destructive_git, pattern_kill, protected_ports, no_foreign_worktree, opt-in claim_required_to_write; each set ask|deny|off per repo in .swarm.toml.

Cursor agent swarm economics (2026-07-20): earlier-2026 browser swarm peaked ~1,000 commits/hour on Git; new system peaks ~1,000 commits/sec; better coordination delivers similar quality at a fraction of the cost.
Stacked review in agent swarms is high-return because review is cheaper than the work it audits; this was a major contributor to sustained quality in Cursor's SQLite-from-scratch experiments.

Swarmery — Go 1.25 binary + React 19 UI, one file, no cloud/account, listens on :7777, data 100% local; backfills sessions from ~/.claude/projects JSONL with zero instrumentation; fail-open hooks shim.

Claude Code's built-in 'Swarms' (feature announced/leaked via HN Jan 2026, 521 pts/335 cmts) ships behind a feature flag that phones home to the backend; delegation mode clears the team-lead context and adds a mailbox for subagent-to-subagent messaging.
Claude Code native agent teams (TeammateTool, inbox communication, tmux split panes) went first-class; previously was feature-flagged and community-built workarounds via subagents and bash scripts.

angles: Local-first control plane as the missing 'observability layer' for the multi-agent age — one daemon watching every session instead of cycling through terminal tabs.
'Stop the collisions': task claims in isolated git worktrees, runtime resources (ports/dev-servers/databases as named singletons), and a collision graph as the core coordination story.

Turning prose guardrails into real permission decisions: CLAUDE.md 'never do X' becomes ask/deny rules returned to Claude Code as actual permission denials (not a sandbox, just guardrails against accidents).
Cost & observability: live token spend, cost-per-turn, cache hit rate, and budgets — the economics angle tied to Cursor's 1,000 commits/sec findings.
Fleet vs swarm: human becomes reviewer/lead delegating to a team, echoing Anthropic's built-in Swarms and the harness-vs-third-party-wrappers debate.
Privacy/sovereignty angle: fully offline, no telemetry, no account — contrasting with built-in Swarms telemetry that captures Claude session JSONL files.
Rapid iteration: eleven releases in weeks, dogfooded daily ('Swarm dispatches its own tasks'), early-but-real status.
